absent: Internal field layout of memory policy, shared policy node, device page map, alternate map and zone structures beyond names referenced in fragments.
Runtime semantics of NUMA balancing enablement, reference counting, completion, read copy update primitives and hotplug exclusion.
Derivation of bandwidth based weights, contents of bandwidth table and interleaving weight query.
Behaviour of helpers for node parsing, string matching, protection conversion, indexed storage, architecture memory add and remove, and page initialization.
Ordering, concurrency and failure handling for concurrent policy updates, sysfs teardown races and device teardown while pages remain busy.
Exact numeric values of mode identifiers, flag bits, error codes, permission bits and subsection size.
Ownership and lifecycle of global policy caches, default policy object and per node preferred array outside early setup.
Sysfs and kernel object core behaviour for creation, lookup and release beyond calls observed.

findings.text: Device memory mapping surface exposes creation of page structures over supplied physical intervals, managed variants tied to device lifetime with automatic teardown, explicit teardown that drains references before releasing address associations, and a query for required alignment.

Memory policy surface offers early initialization of caches and system default, reset to default for current context, conversion from textual mount style description to internal policy object, and rendering of internal policy back to textual form for display.

Boot time control for automatic NUMA balancing accepts enable or disable keywords to record an override, otherwise warns. During early policy setup the override when present forces the global balancing state, and on multi node systems without override the state follows a build time default, while one build variant provides an empty hook with no effect.

Persistent control hierarchy for weighted interleaving appears under memory management controls with a subgroup for weights, per node weight entries created for online memory nodes at startup and added or removed on memory hotplug transitions, plus a single automatic mode control. Failures during construction unwind created objects.
Per node sysfs binding pairs a generic attribute object carrying show and store behaviour with a numeric node identifier used to select which table slot is read or updated.

Group container holds a kernel object for the directory, a mutual exclusion object guarding the table of per node bindings, and a trailing variable length collection of pointers to those bindings indexed by node identifier, with a single global instance.

Weighted interleave shared table is published with read copy update. Writers serialize replacements under a dedicated state mutex and defer reclamation until a grace period, readers sample without that mutex. The directory pointer table is serialized by a separate group mutex held only while checking or linking entries, never across file system removal or memory release.

Device page map address association is published in a global indexed structure with grace period protection after clearing. Hotplug exclusion is held while joining or leaving zones and while adding or removing address mappings. Reference draining uses a per map counter with kill then wait for completion, and teardown iterates all committed intervals.

Balancing override is a boot only integer where positive requests enablement and negative requests disablement. Absence leaves decision to node count and build default, and single node systems leave state untouched when no override is present.

Early policy setup pre creates per node preferred objects with single reference, preferred mode, move related flags and singleton masks. System wide interleave set includes only memory nodes meeting a size threshold, falling back to the largest observed memory node when none qualify, and is installed as the initial interleave configuration before balancing is evaluated.

Textual policy requires mode name lookup with optional flag suffix and optional node list. Node lists must parse and lie within memory nodes. Specific modes constrain presence of lists and defaults, with interleave kinds defaulting to all memory nodes, local forbidding lists, default requiring emptiness and succeeding without allocation, bind like requiring lists, and preferred single restricting numeric form. Flag suffix allows at most one of two mutually exclusive relocation behaviours.

Rendering suppresses internal defaults and per node preferred singletons to the default name. Recognized modes that carry nodes emit stored masks, local and default emit no mask, unknown modes warn and emit a placeholder. Flag suffix appears only when mode flags present, with mutual exclusion between two relocation spellings and an additional balancing marker appended with a separator when combined.

Weight queries return current per node value. Weight updates reject empty input, parse failures and zero, allocate a replacement table sized by possible nodes, preserve existing values or start from unity, install the new weight and leave automatic mode. Automatic mode queries default to true when no table exists. Updates with unchanged mode are no ops, disabling preserves values, enabling requires bandwidth data or fails and derives fresh weights.

Each device interval is rejected when an alternate map accompanies a non initial interval, when either endpoint already has an association, when it overlaps system RAM in whole or part, when indexed publication fails, when protection tracking fails, or when platform permission denies it. Node selection falls back to current memory node when caller passes negative.

Device type determines prerequisites and protection. Private requires build support plus migration and release callbacks and an owner, coherent requires release callback and owner, filesystem DAX uses decrypted protection, generic keeps default kernel protection, peer to peer uses uncached protection, and unrecognized types warn. Empty interval count and oversized map granularity are also rejected.

Interval end in pages derives from byte start plus byte length shifted to pages. Accountable length derives from end minus start further shifted by per map granularity. Successful establishment places pages in the device zone as movable and initializes device page structures. Teardown removes the same span from its zone and detaches architecture mappings or private pages accordingly.

Weighted state moves among absent, manual with explicit weights, and automatic with derived weights. Manual writes and explicit disable enter manual, successful enable enters automatic, identical mode writes stay in place, cleanup and explicit free return to absent. Every transition replaces the whole table object rather than mutating in place.

Mapping establishment starts uncommitted, advances a committed count after each successful interval, and on any failure tears down committed intervals and reports failure while restoring the requested count. Live maps hold extra references per interval except for private and coherent kinds. Teardown kills new references, drains, then releases each interval and completes when the counter reaches zero via a completion signal.

Failure signals include invalid argument for bad text or node identifiers or duplicate entries, no memory for allocation failures, no device when automatic derivation lacks bandwidth data, no such device or address when RAM overlap occurs, plus warnings for conflicting associations, unsupported types, unknown render modes, unparsable boot options and leaked reserve pages on teardown.

Mode identifiers map to display names. Default renders as default, preferred single as prefer, bind as bind, interleave as interleave, weighted interleave as weighted interleave phrase, local as local, preferred many as prefer many phrase.

Hierarchy uses mempolicy directory with weighted interleave child. Per node entries are named by node number with owner write and group and other read permission. Automatic control is named auto with broader write permission. Default weight is one, default automatic reading with no table is true, and zero weight is invalid.

Compatibility alignment equals subsection granularity. Early interleave eligibility threshold equals sixteen megabytes. Preferred singletons start with reference count one and combine two move related flag bits.
